new_entities.name: Metyrapone for Cushing's syndrome
new_entities.description: Metyrapone therapy used to reduce cortisol excess in endogenous Cushing's syndrome, including Cushing's disease.

new_entities.name: Cortisol control
new_entities.description: Reduction or normalization of cortisol excess, usually measured with urinary free cortisol or related cortisol markers.

edges.effect_quant: Metyrapone has a fairly strong cortisol-lowering signal across prospective, retrospective, and pooled evidence. A 2021 meta-analysis estimated disease control in 66% of 66 patients with Cushing's disease, the PROMPT prospective study found normal mean urinary free cortisol in 46.9% by week 12 with 81% meeting the broader response definition, and a 31-patient real-world cohort reported urinary free cortisol normalization in 70% at last follow-up.
edges.population: adults with endogenous Cushing's syndrome, especially pituitary Cushing's disease, treated medically because surgery was not feasible, had failed, or was being bridged
edges.mechanism: Metyrapone inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase, reducing adrenal cortisol synthesis and thereby lowering urinary free cortisol and related markers of hypercortisolism.
edges.summary: This is a protective edge with better real-world consistency than many pituitary-directed drug rows. The efficacy is not universal, but metyrapone routinely lowers cortisol quickly enough to matter clinically.
edges.caveats: The evidence base includes uncontrolled studies and mixes Cushing's disease with broader endogenous Cushing's syndrome populations. Control rates also depend on how strictly response is defined and whether LC-MS/MS or immunoassay endpoints are used.

evidence.citation: Simoes Correa Galendi J et al 2021 Front Endocrinol (Lausanne)
evidence.notes: Effectiveness of Medical Treatment of Cushing's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: pooled proportion of Cushing disease control with metyrapone across included studies

evidence.citation: Daniel E et al 2025 Eur J Endocrinol
evidence.notes: Prospective study of metyrapone in endogenous Cushing's syndrome (PROMPT).
